subject: Private connectivity readiness — egress patterns, PrivateLink preference & next tech steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@netatlas.com>, Samir Desai <samir.desai@netatlas.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private connectivity readiness — egress patterns, PrivateLink preference & next tech steps

Hi Priya / Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the Private VPC workstream.

Call recap (high level):
- NetAtlas is leaning toward a Private VPC deployment for production due to data residency and audit requirements; early PoC may use Dedicated for speed.
- Security team prefers PrivateLink over VPC peering where possible, but they asked for clarification on egress ownership and IP allowlist expectations.
- Network team (Samir) will own firewall/NAT details, but asked Redwood for a concise checklist of ports/paths and example IP ranges to expect from our control plane.

Requested next steps from Redwood:
1) Share a one-page PrivateLink vs peering tradeoff summary (security/management implications).
2) Provide the minimal egress/ingress port list and the static IP ranges (or ranges by region) customers need to allowlist.
3) Attach a short checklist (network diagram + ownership table) we can use with NetAtlas NetOps.

Ben / Vivek — looping you in to draft the checklist and sample IPs. Ben, can you attach the technical checklist and note which network flows must remain open for telemetry/health checks? Vivek, can you confirm whether Redwood requires a fixed set of outbound IPs for PrivateLink control-plane callbacks (or if customers will see region-specific ranges)?

Priya / Samir — let me know if I'm missing anything obvious. If it helps, we can schedule a 30-minute NetOps deep dive next week to walk the diagram.

Thanks,
Olga
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_privatelink_checklist_v1.pdf)

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@netatlas.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Desai <samir.desai@netatlas.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private connectivity readiness — egress patterns, PrivateLink preference & next tech steps

Hi Olga — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before the deep-dive:

1) PrivateLink preference: Our security/compliance team prefers PrivateLink because it avoids transitive routing between VPCs and matches our audit controls. If Redwood requires peering for any feature, we need the justification and a risk mitigation plan.

2) Egress model: For most workloads we terminate outbound calls through a central NAT/proxy in our shared services VPC. That means Redwood will see egress from a narrow set of NAT IPs (we can provide these once we confirm the environment), but for some test/pooled envs we may use ephemeral egress.

3) Allowlist expectation: Security wants a short list (<= 10) of CIDR blocks or static IPs per region for control-plane and telemetry. We cannot accept a dynamic range that changes per deployment without a change control window.

4) Network diagram: attaching our high-level diagram (netatlas-network-diagram.png). Samir, can you add the NAT/pool CIDRs you plan to expose? Also we need to know whether Redwood's PrivateLink requires any inbound port openings beyond standard HTTPS (443).

If we can get the checklist and sample IPs this week, I can route them to Compliance and NetOps for sign-off and then we can lock a date for the technical workshop.

Thanks,
Priya
Director, Cloud Security — NetAtlas
(attachment: netatlas-network-diagram.png)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@netatlas.com>, Samir Desai <samir.desai@netatlas.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-19T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private connectivity readiness — egress patterns, PrivateLink preference & next tech steps

Priya / Samir — thanks for the diagram and context. A few concrete answers and an attached checklist that matches the items Olga listed. Key points below (short):

- PrivateLink vs Peering: PrivateLink is fully supported for our control plane and TLS traffic. Peering is only required for extremely high-throughput KV cache replication patterns and is optional for most customers. We'll mark those features explicitly in the checklist so you can decide.

- Required ports: outbound HTTPS (443) for control plane and model fetches; TCP 443 for telemetry/metrics ingestion; optionally TCP 22 for initial troubleshooting if you open a jump host (rare). We do NOT require any additional inbound ports on customer VPCs for standard PrivateLink.

- IP allowlist: For US region PoCs, Redwood control-plane egress uses a published set of static IPs. Example (pooled): 34.215.12.0/28, 34.215.12.16/28, 54.183.98.0/28. For production PrivateLink endpoints, each endpoint is a private ENI — no public IPs to allowlist; however our control plane callbacks originate from the static control-plane IPs above for webhook callbacks (if you opt into them).

- Health/heartbeat: We recommend opening outbound connections to our telemetry endpoint (https://telemetry.redwood.ai/ingest) over 443. Heartbeat interval is configurable (default 30s) — we'll include this in the checklist.

Attached: redwood_privatelink_checklist_v1.pdf (includes a short feature matrix, ports, sample IP ranges, and ownership table).

Next asks from NetAtlas: if you can provide the NAT/pool CIDRs and whether you operate an outbound proxy (hostname + ip) we can map exact flows. Also confirm whether compliance needs signed attestations or SOC2 evidence — we can pull the appropriate artifacts once we have the scope.

If helpful, I'm available for the NetOps deep-dive on Tue/Wed next week between 10–2 PT.

—Ben
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_privatelink_checklist_v1.pdf)

From: Samir Desai <samir.desai@netatlas.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@netatlas.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private connectivity readiness — egress patterns, PrivateLink preference & next tech steps

Thanks team — this is helpful. Quick answers from NetOps:

- NAT/pool CIDRs (test envs): 10.200.8.0/24 (ephemeral), 10.200.9.0/28 (reserved PoC NAT egress).
- Prod shared NAT egress (will provide specific public IPs after change control window) — plan is to surface up to 6 static IPs per region.
- We confirm we run an outbound proxy at proxy.netatlas.internal:8080 for some workloads — we'll list which clusters use it in the doc.

We can do the deep-dive Tuesday 2026-09-28 at 10:30 PT — calendar invite to follow. Please include the checklist and the PrivateLink tradeoff summary in the invite so NetOps has pre-read.

Samir
Senior Network Engineer — NetAtlas
